Per AI:

Nvidia + Intel: Building the Complete AI Computing Company

The strongest case for combining Nvidia and Intel is to unite computing architecture, software and manufacturing under one strategy. The opportunity extends from AI data centers to enterprise servers and personal computers.

The companies already have a commercial foundation. Their announced collaboration combines Intel’s x86 CPUs with Nvidia technology for data center and PC products. A merger would seek to turn that partnership into a coordinated platform with shared investment priorities and product development.

1. Design the entire system together

AI performance depends on how processors, memory, networking and software work together. Combined ownership could allow engineering teams to optimize across those boundaries, align development schedules and reduce conflicting commercial priorities.

The customer proposition would be measurable: faster deployment, better performance per watt and lower total operating costs.

2. Give Intel Foundry a powerful anchor customer

Nvidia could provide a potential source of manufacturing demand, technical collaboration and investment confidence for Intel Foundry. In return, Nvidia could gain another manufacturing option and greater influence over future process and packaging development.

That opportunity must remain conditional on competitive yields, cost and delivery. Moving production prematurely would destroy value.

3. Expand distribution across computing markets

Intel brings extensive relationships across PC manufacturers and enterprise computing. Nvidia brings accelerated computing and its software ecosystem. Together, they could develop integrated products and sell more capabilities through existing customer channels.

4. Fund manufacturing with disciplined investment

The strategic argument is that Nvidia’s earnings capacity could support selected Intel manufacturing investments. Management would need strict spending milestones, accountable leadership and clear returns rather than an open-ended commitment to factory expansion.

5. Strengthen supply resilience

A competitive US manufacturing alternative could become valuable to customers seeking geographic diversification. That could support long-term supply agreements, although domestic production would still depend on international equipment, materials and other suppliers.

Structure the deal around accountability

The combined company should preserve Intel Foundry as a separately governed business with customer confidentiality protections. Product divisions should retain clear profit responsibility, while leadership integrates architecture, software and sales where benefits can be demonstrated.

The investment decision

Proceed only if the acquisition premium, integration costs and manufacturing investment are outweighed by credible operating benefits. The decisive question is whether ownership delivers advantages that contracts cannot reliably secure.

Done well, the combination could create a broader, more resilient computing platform—and give customers a compelling reason to buy it.
